question: ‘Purusha Sukta’ is a hymn from which Veda?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Rigveda.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **‘Purusha Sukta’ is a hymn from Rigveda.**
 
• In the **10th Mandala** of the Rigveda, Purusha Sukta outlines the origin of the four varnas (Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Shudra) from different parts of Purusha’s body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **About Rig Veda**:

 
 
• Rig Veda was said to be composed between 1500-1200 B.C, also known as the first testament of mankind.
 
• It is a collection of 10,600 verses and 1,028 hymns.
 
• It consists of 10 books also known as mandalas, each Mandal consists of Suktas.
 
• It consists of various secrets about the origin of the universe, the origin of Lord Shiva, the origin of Lord Varuna, etc.
